title: DL-TerrainSlicer: digital terrain models to laser-ready DXF files for stacked contour models
description:
Turns a digital terrain model into laser-ready DXF files for a stacked cardboard contour model, using the horizontal contour offset method: the terrain is sliced into contour levels at material-thickness intervals and distributed onto N boards, board k carrying contours k, k+N, k+2N, … as in-place cutlines, so every contour is cut exactly once and the pieces are rings rather than solid slabs. Output is one DXF per material sheet with one layer per laser pass, plus a cutting report.

Reads GeoTIFF terrain models and OBJ terrain meshes; polygon, line and point shapefiles become hatching, scored linework and circles. Contour numbers are engraved in single-stroke Hershey fonts, hidden in the glue zone by default.

Runs as a desktop application (Windows, macOS) or entirely in the browser (Pyodide/WebAssembly); terrain data is processed locally and never transmitted. A standalone replacement for a Grasshopper definition — no Rhino, no GDAL, no GIS licence.
